== Research status ==

This page is based on John Glasgw's testament testamentar and inventory in the Glasgow Commissary Court records. Further research is needed to identify his parents, exact birth date, wife, and the names of his children.

== Biography ==
Johne Glasgw was a [https://www.glasgowlife.org.uk/libraries/city-archives/archive-collections burgess] of Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland, living in the early 17th century. Glasgow City Archives holds the city's surviving burgess rolls, although its published description notes that the series begins in 1573 and is incomplete. His exact birth date and parentage are currently unknown.

He was alive on 7 April 1637 when he personally made his last will and testament, likely while suffering from complications of a leg injury, as he owed money to a surgeon for its cure. He died shortly thereafter, in April 1637, certainly by the 17th of April when his testament was formally dated, and specifically stated to have occurred on the 7th of April 1637 later in the document regarding provision for his children. <ref name="NRS_Will">National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, The Testament Testamentar and Inventar of Johne Glasgw, burgess of Glasgow, 17 April 1637, Reference CC9/7/27, Images 478, 479, 480.</ref>

=== Occupation ===
John was described as a "burges of glasgw". His associates and creditors included several merchants ("merchand burges"), suggesting he may also have been involved in trade. <ref name="NRS_Will"/>

=== Family ===
The testament confirms John had children ("bairnes"), as provision was made for their maintenance ("Intertenyment") from the date of his death (7 April 1637) until the processing of the testament. The cost allocated was £60 Scots.<ref name="NRS_Will"/> The names and number of children are not specified.

The division of his free estate ("frie geir") into only two parts ("Twa pairtis" - the Defunct's Part and implicitly the Bairns' Part) suggests that his wife likely predeceased him. If she had survived, the estate would typically have been divided into three parts (spouse, bairns, defunct).<ref name="NRS_Will"/> His wife's name is not mentioned.

=== Testament and Estate ===
John Glasgw made his will ("Testament testamen / tar") on 7 April 1637, before witnesses Johne Bell elder (merchant burgess of Glasgow) and Robert Stewart (merchant burgess of Glasgow).<ref name="NRS_Will"/>

==== Inventory and Debts ====
The inventory primarily consisted of one debt owed *to* the deceased:
* From the late (vmquhile) Johne Corsbie, merchant burgess of Glasgow: £42 13s 4d Scots.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>

The debts owed *by* the deceased were substantial and meticulously listed:
* To James Bell elder, merchant burgess of Glasgow: £65.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>
* To Johne Sobcoll [Scobell?]: £33 (for rent of lands called "Provest hauch", to be paid in 1638).<ref name="NRS_Will"/>
* To James Maxwell, Costadoune: £12.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>
* To Agnes Paull, spouse to Patrik Park: Amount possibly combined or unspecified, listed just before John Stark.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>
* To Johne Stark, officer in Renfrew ("Runfre[w]"): £15 5s.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>
* To "Maltman", his apprentice ("prenteis"): £40 (for apprentice fee and other accounts).<ref name="NRS_Will"/>
* Funeral Expenses:
** To George Kay, draper (for mourning clothes): £30.
** To Williame Hervie (for "stuff"): £8 13s 4d.
** To Jonet Broun (for wine and spicery): £50.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>
* Support for his children ("bairnes") from 7 April 1637 until the testament date: £60.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>
* To James Andersone, surgeon ("chirurgian") (for curing a hurt leg): £10.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>
* To Johne Bell, merchant burgess of Glasgow (presumably the elder witness) (for house rent - "house maill"): £8.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>
* To Robert Stewart, merchant burgess of Glasgow (the other witness and executor) (for certain debts): £7 13s 4d.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>
* To Johne Maxwell elder (possibly the cautioner mentioned later) (for house rent - "house maill"): £8.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>

==== Estate Summary ====
* Total Debts Owed By John: £255 6s 8d Scots.
* Free Gear (Net Estate after debts): £3 6s 8d Scots.
* Defunct's Part (portion disposable by will): £1 13s 4d Scots.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>

==== Executor and Legacy ====
John nominated Robert Stewart, merchant burgess of Glasgow (who was also a witness to the will), as his sole executor ("onlie executor testamentar & Intromittor"). Robert was instructed to pay all the debts first, and then to dispose of the remaining small surplus (£1 13s 4d) "To him selff".<ref name="NRS_Will"/>

=== Death and Probate ===
John Glasgw died in Glasgow in April 1637, stated specifically as the 7th of April 1637.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>

His testament was signed "Jon glasgw" and notarized by Joannes Hutchesone, Notary Public. The witnesses, Johne Bell and Robert Stewart, also signed.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>

The testament was formally confirmed ("Confirmatio") by the Commissary Court of Glasgow on 27 April 1637 ("vigesimo Septimo die mensis aprillis Anno domini millesimo Sexcentesimo trigesimo Septimo"). The judge was Robertus hammiltoun (Robert Hamilton), Commissary.<ref name="NRS_Will"/>

Robert Stewart formally accepted the role of executor, taking an oath that the inventory was accurate and that he would faithfully manage the estate. Cautioners (guarantors) appointed for Robert Stewart's execution of his duties were Johne Bell senior, merchant burgess of Glasgow (likely the witness) and Johne Maxwell senior, burgess of Glasgow (likely the one owed rent).<ref name="NRS_Will"/>
